name: Lao

allophone_rules.notes: Lao permits only /p t k m n ŋ w j/ in the coda, and every coronal obstruent letter neutralises there to an unreleased [t̚]: ⟨ລົດ⟩ is /lot̚/ and ⟨ວັດ⟩ /ʋat̚/, not *[lod]/*[ʋad]. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao. Gated on syllable_position=coda so onset /d/ is untouched (⟨ດີ⟩ stays /diː/).
Labial coda neutralisation, the labial half of the same rule: ⟨ຮັບ⟩ is /hap̚/. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao. Coda-gated, so onset /b/ is untouched.
Velar coda neutralisation, the velar half of the same rule: ⟨ດອກ⟩ is /dɔːk̚/. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao.
⟨ຍ⟩ is the palatal nasal /ɲ/ in the onset but the glide /j/ in the coda, the only position a Lao syllable admits it: ⟨ຂ້ອຍ⟩ is /kʰɔːj/. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao.

Lao /ʋ/ is a labiodental approximant in the onset and the glide [w] in the coda, where the labiodental articulation is not available: ⟨ລາວ⟩ is /laːw/ against onset ⟨ວັດ⟩ /ʋat̚/. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao.

⟨ອ⟩ has two jobs. After an onset consonant it is the vowel letter /ɔː/ (⟨ດອກ⟩ /dɔːk̚/); when it opens a syllable of its own it is the zero-consonant carrier that a vowel sign needs to attach to, and is read as the glottal onset (⟨ອິດ⟩ /ʔit̚/). The following vowel is what distinguishes the two, so the rule is gated on the grapheme AND on a following vowel. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao.

notes:
Lao, the Southwestern Tai language of Laos, written in its own Indic-derived abugida. The spec describes the Vientiane standard.

Vowels are written with signs that stand before, above, below or after their consonant, and several are circumfixes. The preposed signs are ⟨ເ ແ ໂ ໃ ໄ⟩: they precede the consonant on the page and follow it in speech, so ⟨ເກ⟩ is /keː/. A circumfix pairs one of them with a post-consonantal part, which is what the multi-character vowel keys ⟨ືອ ຶອ ົາ ົວ າະ⟩ encode: ⟨ເສືອ⟩ 'tiger' is /sɯːə/, ⟨ເຮົາ⟩ 'we' is /haw/, ⟨ເກາະ⟩ 'island' is /kɔʔ/. ⟨ະ⟩ writes short /a/ in an open syllable and carries the glottal check Lao gives such syllables; ⟨ັ⟩ and ⟨ົ⟩ write short /a/ and /o/ in a closed one.

A Lao syllable may close only on /p t k m n ŋ w j/. Every other consonant letter neutralises in the coda, which the LO_CODA_* rules encode: coronal obstruents to unreleased [t̚], labials to [p̚], velars to [k̚], and ⟨ຍ⟩ from onset /ɲ/ to the glide /j/. The rules are gated on the coda, so the onset readings are untouched — ⟨ດີ⟩ is /diː/ while ⟨ລົດ⟩ is /lot̚/. Lao likewise admits no liquid coda. The inventory is declared in `codas` and used only to refuse a coda reading of a ho-nam tail after a preposed vowel; no rule rewrites a word-final liquid, and a measurement of the kaikki gold says why. Nine words end in ⟨ລ⟩ or ⟨ຣ⟩. Six of the nine have the letter as the ONSET of a final syllable whose vowel is a preposed sign (⟨ກິໂລ⟩ /kiʔ.loː/, ⟨ທະເລ⟩ /tʰa.leː/, ⟨ກຳໄລ⟩ /kam.laj/) or is the subscript of a word-final ho-nam ⟨ຫຼ⟩ (⟨ໄຫລ⟩ /laj/), so a positional rule that fires word-finally reads an onset as a coda in two productive spelling classes and breaks ⟨ໄຫລ⟩, which is currently correct. The remaining three are not one phenomenon and none of them is a liquid the engine could simply neutralise. ⟨ນຄຣ⟩ and ⟨ທຫາຣ⟩ are abbreviated etymological Indic spellings of ⟨ນະຄອນ⟩ /naʔ.kʰɔːn/ and ⟨ທະຫານ⟩ /tʰaʔ.haːn/ — both fully spelled forms are in the same gold and this spec already reads both correctly — so reading them needs the unwritten ⟨ະ⟩ and ⟨ອ⟩ supplied, which no rule about the final letter provides. ⟨ອີແມລ⟩ is the English loan 'email' whose final /l/ is nativised to /n/, a loan-adaptation fact about one word. Three words spread over two unrelated causes do not establish a coda rule, and the rule they would motivate costs more spellings than it fixes.

⟨ຫ⟩ before a sonorant is not an /h/ but the ho nam tone-class marker: the sonorant is the onset and the ⟨ຫ⟩ only shifts the syllable into the high class, so ⟨ຫລອດ⟩ is /lɔːt̚/ and ⟨ຫມາ⟩ /maː/. ⟨ໝ⟩ and ⟨ໜ⟩ are single-codepoint ligatures of the same device, and ⟨ຫຼ⟩ writes it with the subscript lo ⟨ຼ⟩. Before a vowel ⟨ຫ⟩ is a real /h/ (⟨ຫໍ⟩ /hɔː/), which is why the marker is encoded as digraphs rather than as a silencing of ⟨ຫ⟩. After a preposed vowel the tail stays the onset when it is a liquid, because no liquid closes a Lao syllable: ⟨ອາໂຫລ⟩ and ⟨ອາໂຫຼ⟩ are /ʔaːloː/.

⟨ວ⟩ is the labiodental approximant /ʋ/ in the onset and the glide /w/ in the coda. ⟨ຣ⟩ is read /l/, the ho-nam digraph ⟨ຫຣ⟩ with it: the historical /r/ has merged with /l/ in the modern language. ⟨ອ⟩ is the vowel /ɔː/ after an onset and the zero-consonant carrier /ʔ/ when it opens a syllable itself.

A consonant letter with no vowel sign on it carries the inherent vowel /o/, the value it takes in the closed syllables such a spelling writes (⟨ຄນ⟩ /kʰon/).

Lao has no lexical word stress — prominence is carried by the tone system — so no `stress` block is encoded (research-tier exemption). Tone itself is not written into the IPA: it is a property of the syllable computed from the consonant class and the tone marks ⟨່ ້ ໊ ໋⟩, which are recorded in `tone_inventory` and mapped to nothing segmentally. Measured against the kaikki gold as fetched on 2026-09-28, the snapshot the board row scores at n=2312: 747 of the 2313 loaded rows carry a tone mark, and every gold transcription carries a tone letter. So the contrast is written, it survives into the scored input, and the gold transcribes it; what is missing is a `tone_rules` block. The engine already computes syllable-level tone from one: `ToneRules` is built for Tai-style systems, `assign_computed_tones` names no language, and `th` is the one spec that uses it. The residual on that row is open work, not a limit of the writing system. The circumfixes whose post-consonantal part is ambiguous on its own — ⟨ເ◌ັ⟩ /e/, ⟨ແ◌ັ⟩ /ɛ/, ⟨ເ◌ີ⟩ /ɤː/ — are NOT encoded, because the vowel key cannot see which preposed sign it belongs to; encoding them by position would be fitting the benchmark rather than describing the orthography. Neither is the cancellation mark ⟨໌⟩, which silences the letter it stands on (⟨ວຽງຈັນທນ໌⟩ /ʋiːəŋtɕan/): it is mapped to nothing itself, but the letter it kills is still read.

One known gap. ⟨ເ...ອ⟩ is a preposed-sign/⟨ອ⟩ circumfix like ⟨ເ◌ີ⟩ above and is likewise NOT encoded for the same reason: ⟨ເສອ⟩ reads sɔː, dropping the preposed /eː/ that the circumfix as a whole gives (⟨ໂອເຊອານີ⟩ 'Oceania' loses its second syllable's nucleus). Separately, a reading is encoded through `consonant_nuclei`: a bare ⟨ວ⟩ between an unvowelled onset and a closing consonant is the nucleus /uːə/, the vowel ⟨ົວ⟩ spells with its sign (⟨ພວກ⟩ is /pʰuːək̚/, ⟨ກວດ⟩ /kuːət̚/, ⟨ຫລວງ⟩ /luːəŋ/). The string is the Kaikki gold's nucleus ⟨uːə̯⟩ with the offglide mark dropped, which is how this spec already writes ⟨ົວ⟩; Enfield 2007 was not consulted for it. Of the 2,316 Kaikki gold words, 46 spell the shape ⟨consonant + ວ + consonant⟩ (the first consonant may carry the subscript ⟨ຼ⟩) with no vowel sign after the second consonant. 43 carry ⟨uːə̯⟩ in the gold. The other 3 (⟨ແຂວງ⟩, ⟨ແຫວນ⟩, ⟨ສະແຫວງ⟩) carry a preposed ⟨ແ⟩ that makes ⟨ວ⟩ its own onset or coda, so the reading must not reach them and does not. The reading yields the nucleus in 24 of the 43. 19 stay unread, for two reasons. 8 begin the shape with ⟨ຫຼ⟩ (⟨ຫຼວງ⟩, ⟨ທາງຫຼວງ⟩, ⟨ຕຳຫຼວດ⟩): the engine treats a key ending in a combining mark, here the semivowel sign ⟨ຼ⟩, as a bare mark and does not test the letter after it, so ⟨ຫຼວງ⟩ is still /lʋoŋ/ while the gold-equivalent spelling ⟨ຫລວງ⟩ is /luːəŋ/. The other 11 (⟨ຄຳນວນ⟩, ⟨ຈຳນວນ⟩, ⟨ສື່ມວນຊົນ⟩, ⟨ຂະບວນການ⟩, ⟨ກະຊວງ⟩ and six more) stand after an earlier syllable that has a vowel, and the shared mechanism cannot tell the onset of a new syllable from the coda of the old one there, so they keep ⟨ວ⟩ as /ʋ/.

CODA INVENTORY. `codas` lists /p̚ t̚ k̚ ʔ m n ŋ w j/, the segments that close a Lao syllable, and the tokenizer uses it to refuse a coda reading of a ho-nam tail after a preposed vowel. The list is measured on the Kaikki gold, not taken from a grammar: of the 4,711 syllables in its 2,316 words, the final consonants are n 631, ŋ 473, t̚ 451, j 317, m 316, k̚ 290, p̚ 218, ʔ 214, w 199 and s 7, and l and r close none. The 7 syllables ending in s are unassimilated loans (ອີສເຕີ, ອາລາສກາ, ໄວຣັສ). Enfield 2007 is the standing description in this spec's bibliography; it was not consulted for this list.
